Migration

What it means, and what it does to a claim.

Moving to a different policy with the same insurer while keeping the waiting-period credit you have already built up. A group plan to an individual one, or an old product to a current one.

Why it matters

This is the route out of employer group cover when you leave a job. Done at the right moment, the years you spent covered under the group policy still count. Done late, they do not, and you start over as a new customer in your forties instead of your twenties.

The legal definition

Migration means a facility provided to policyholders (including all members under family cover and group policies), to transfer the credits gained for pre-existing diseases and specific waiting periods from one health insurance policy to another with the same insurer.

Aditya Birla Health — Activ One policy wording, UIN ADIHLIP27048V022627

Quoted verbatim from an IRDAI-filed policy wording. Definitions are standardised across insurers, but the limits attached to them are not — always read your own policy schedule.

Related terms

  • Break in Policy — A gap between one policy period ending and the next beginning, because the premium was not paid in time.
  • Portability — Moving your health policy to a different insurer without losing the waiting periods you have already served.
  • Waiting Period — A stretch of time at the start of a policy when certain conditions are not covered yet.
